union.text: Arles, where Constantine III was besieged until August-September 411

land.text: Gaul except Armorica and Arles, the land of Constantine III's Rhine army

predecessors.note: The Rhine army of Constantine III 'abandoned him to support yet another claimant to the imperial throne' (Constantine III page, 411, undated within the year); Jovinus was 'proclaimed emperor at Mainz in 411', 'Following the defeat of the usurper known as Constantine III' (Jovinus page). Constantine III kept only Arles until his execution in August-September 411.

land.text: Gaul, held 'for about two years' (Jovinus page), cut to the Western Roman Empire's 406 shape

successors.note: Ataulf's Visigoths allied with Honorius and 'defeated Jovinus's troops'; Jovinus was captured at Valence and executed at Narbonne in 413. The Visigoths and Burgundians (who settled on the Rhine's left bank 'between the Lauter and the Nahe') keep their own land.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'He held Gaul for about two years' (Jovinus page); the Burgundians of Gundahar settled 'on the Rhine's left bank, between the Lauter and the Nahe'. The page names no cities except Mainz, Valence and Narbonne and gives no extent or area. Gaul cut to the Western Roman Empire's 406 shape is a maximum. Repair fx-28: Arles is left out because Constantine III still held it, besieged, until he was beheaded 'in either August or September 411' (Constantine III page), and the rest of Gaul comes from Constantine III, whose Rhine troops 'abandoned him to support yet another claimant to the imperial throne' (Constantine III page); Jovinus was proclaimed 'Following the defeat of the usurper known as Constantine III' (Jovinus page). Constantine III is therefore a predecessor.

'Insulted, Ataulf allied his Visigoths with Honorius,' and they defeated Jovinus's troops; he was 'besieged and captured in Valentia' (Valence, Drome) and taken to Narbonne, where Claudius Postumus Dardanus 'had him executed'. The infobox gives 413; the body gives no year for the capture.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, requested by the eu-04-b report ('Jovinus (usurper in Gaul)', 411-413) and by the constantine-iii-usurper dossier. One page opened (page budget: the Constantine III page used by the neighbouring dossier was not re-opened); it dates the proclamation (411, Mainz) and the end (413) but not the capture of Valence or the spread of his rule, so the shape is a maximum (Gaul within the Western Roman Empire's 406 shape) and the counterpart 'visigoths' is the Cliopatria Visigoths row.
